guideposts.label: A new stage town on the map of La Vuelta ahead of a classic finish
guideposts.detail: Palma del Rio make its debut as La Vuelta stage town* while Cordoba is a classic venue about to witness a 23rd finish. There are three Andalusian riders in the peloton of La Vuelta 26 (Carlos Rodriguez, Cristian Rodriguez, José Manuel Diaz Gallego) but none of them is from the province of Cordoba. The most emblematic rider from the area is Antonio Gomez del Moral (from Cabra, 75 km south of Cordob

guideposts.label: The last 2 winners in Cordoba can repeat success today
guideposts.detail: In 2021, Magnus Cort dominated a reduced bunch sprint to take the 2nd of his 3 stage wins that year. In 2024, Wout van Aert dominated a reduced bunch sprint to take the 2nd of his 3 stage wins that year. Sepp Kuss was essential to propel him to the victory. Pau Miquel was 3rd. guideposts.label: Cort: "I expect a breakaway to go to the finish today"
guideposts.detail: Magnus Cort (Uno-X Mobility) won in Cordoba in 2021: "I have good memories. It was not a stage I planned to try to win that year, I was in the breakaway the day before so I was taking it easy all day long in the peloton. Suddenly everything came back together for a sprint and I won. I think it can be a reduced bunch sprint but I expect a breakaway to go to the finish today."

guideposts.label: Team standings
guideposts.detail: XDS Astanahad the best collective performance yesterday and moved up to the second place of the overall team standings, 1h02’02’’ behind Decathlon CMA CGM. Bahrain Victorious are third (+1h12’12’’).

guideposts.label: A fast pace from the get go
guideposts.detail: With a series of attacks and counter-attacks, the riders have already covered 5 kilometres.

guideposts.label: Paleni insists
guideposts.detail: Among the most active riders so far today, Enzo Paleni (Groupama-FDJ United) has opened a small gap at km 10. Counter-attackers try to chase him down as they enter the final 100 kilometres of the stage.

guideposts.label: The gap drops down to 50 seconds on the climb
guideposts.detail: Steven Kruijswijk (Visma-Lease a Bike) currently sets the pace.

guideposts.label: The breakaway
Steinhauser attacks
guideposts.detail: Georg Steinhauser (EF Education-EasyPost) sets off from the bunch to try and bridge the 50'' gap to the leaders in the last kilometre of ascent.

guideposts.label: Leemreize leads the way to the summit with minimal gaps
guideposts.detail: +17'' Steinhauser +33'' Peloton, now paced by Armirail

guideposts.label: Steinhauser joins the breakaway
guideposts.detail: The peloton are only 25 seconds behind with 70 kilometres to go.

guideposts.label: 41.8 km covered in the first hour
guideposts.detail: As expected, the pace is relentless today. The last gap: 30 seconds.

guideposts.label: Primoz Roglic swaps bikes on a downhill
guideposts.detail: The Slovenian won La Vuelta the last two times Cordoba hosted a stage finish, in 2021 and 2024.

guideposts.label: Marco Brenner became the 32nd rider to win a Grand Tour stage in 2026
guideposts.detail: With Marco Brenner taking his maiden Grand Tour stage win as well as Tudor’s first, 32 riders from 17 teams and representing 15 nations have won Grand Tour stages this year. 8 stage wins - Tadej Pogacar 5 - Jonas Vingegaard 3 - Matthew Brennan, Paul Magnier, Tim Merlier, Jhonatan Narvaez 2 - Richard Carapaz, Remco Evenepoel, Mathieu van der Poel 1 - Wout van Aert, Igor Arrieta, Davide Ballerini, A

guideposts.label: 2026 Grand Tour stage wins by teams
guideposts.detail: 13 - UAE Emirates XRG 11 - Visma-Lease a Bike 6 - Soudal Quick-Step 3 - Alpecin-Premier Tech, EF Education-EasyPost, Uno-X Mobility, XDS Astana 2 - Bahrain Victorious, Lidl-Trek, Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe 1 - Cofidis, Decathlon CMA CGM, Groupama-FDJ United, Jayco AlUla, Movistar, Netcompany Ineos, Tudor UAE Emirates XRG, Visma-Lease a Bike and Uno-X Mobility have won stages in the three Grand Tours.

guideposts.label: 2026 Grand Tour stage wins by nations
guideposts.detail: 9 - Slovenia 8 - Belgium 7 - Denmark 5 - Ecuador, France 4 - Italy, Netherlands 3 - Great Britain, Norway 2 - Spain 1 - Germany, Mexico, Switzerland, Uruguay, USA

guideposts.label: 50 kilometres to go
guideposts.detail: The route is up and down through the Sierra de Hornachuelos. The last gap: 30 seconds.

guideposts.label: New attacks
guideposts.detail: After Novak's acceleration, Michael Gogl (Alpecin-Premier Tech) attacks with 48 km to go. The Austrian national champion is 20 seconds behind the leaders.

guideposts.label: Enric Mas (Movistar)
Leknessund sets a strong pace into the final 40 kilometres
guideposts.detail: Only Azparren can follow the Norwegian, already a stage winner at Aramon Valdelinares (stage 7). Debruyne joins Paleni and Steinhauser in pursuit. The peloton are 20 seconds behind.

guideposts.label: Bruno Armirail (Visma | Lease a Bike)
Debruyne joins Leknessund
guideposts.detail: The duo face the final 33 kilometres with a gap of 20 seconds to the bunch.

guideposts.label: Ramses Debruyne and Andreas Leknessund
Debruyne goes first at the intermediate; Van Aert attacks!
guideposts.detail: The Belgian icon was fourth at the line, and he kept pushing. He joins the lead duo with 30.5 km to go. Alessandro Romele and Thibau Nys follow.

guideposts.label: The situation into the final 30 kilometres
guideposts.detail: Van Aert, Nys, Debruyne, Leknessund and Romele lead the way. +12'' Fisher-Black, Johannessen +23'' Peloton

guideposts.label: Paleni and Tronchon attack from the bunch
guideposts.detail: Groupama-FDJ United want to put Bastien Tronchon in a position to repeat the victory he took in Elche de la Sierra (stage 10).

guideposts.label: The leaders are 21 km from the finish
guideposts.detail: +45'' Chase group +1'05'' Paleni and Tronchon +1'25'' Peloton

guideposts.label: The pace drops in the bunch
guideposts.detail: With 20 kilometres remaining, the gap increases to 1'55''.

guideposts.label: 15 kilometres to go
guideposts.detail: The five leaders are on the downhill ahead of the final run-in to Cordoba. The chase group are 45 seconds behind.

guideposts.label: Nys attacks with 3 km to go
guideposts.detail: Debruyne is on his wheel. Van Aert reacts to close the gap.

guideposts.label: Leknessund counter-attacks...
guideposts.detail: Van Aert is vigilant.

guideposts.label: Wout van Aert wins stage 15 of La Vuelta 26!
guideposts.detail: His second victory in La Vuelta 26, and his second victory in Cordoba after 2024!

guideposts.label: Top 5
guideposts.detail: 1. Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike) 2. Alessandro Romele (XDS Astana) 3. Thibau Nys (Lidl-Trek) 4. Ramses Debruyne (Alpecin-Premier Tech) 5. Andreas Leknessund (Uno-X Mobility)
